content: 1. Chang OH, Levy B, Lytle H, Pope R, Phiri H, Gellhaus T, et al. conducted a study on the implementation of the Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health Program in Malawi. This program aimed to reduce maternal mortality rates. The findings were published in Obstetrics & Gynecology in 2019, volume 133, issue 3, pages 507–514. 2. Davidson C, Denning S, Thorp K, Tyer-Viola L, Belfort M, Sangi-Haghpeykar H, et al. examined the impact of quality improvement initiatives on reducing racial disparities in maternal morbidity. Their research was published in BMJ Quality & Safety in 2022, volume 31, issue 9, pages 670–678. 3. Duzyj CM, Boyle C, Mahoney K, Johnson AR, Ogot G, Ayers C reported on the implementation of a postpartum hemorrhage patient safety bundle at a single institution. They discussed the successes, failures, and lessons learned. The study appeared in the American Journal of Perinatology in 2021, volume 38, issue 12, pages 1281–1288. 4. Hamm RF, Wang E, O’Rourke K, Romanos A, Srinivas SK evaluated the introduction of a comprehensive postpartum hemorrhage bundle at a large academic center. They found that it did not immediately reduce maternal morbidity. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Perinatology in 2019, volume 36, issue 1, pages 15–21. 5. Kotze A, Adam Y, Naidoo P investigated maternal outcomes before and after the implementation of a new oxytocin protocol during cesarean deliveries. Their study was published in the International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics in 2022, volume 158, issue 2, pages 368–376. 6. Seim AR, Alassoum Z, Souley I, Bronzan R, Mounkaila A, Ahmed LA conducted a 72-month longitudinal study in Niger to assess the effects of a peripartum strategy aimed at preventing and treating primary postpartum hemorrhage in health facilities. The results were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2023, volume 11, issue 2, pages e287–e295. 7. Sleutel MR, Newcomb P, Elling C, Beaverstock L, Peron T studied the effect of an obstetric hemorrhage bundle on clinical outcomes and clinician perceptions. Their findings were published in Nursing for Women’s Health in 2021, volume 25, issue 4, pages 248–256. 8. Sullivan J, Rockhill K, Larrea N, Fabbri S analyzed the prevalence of blood product transfusion following the implementation of a postpartum hemorrhage bundle. This retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single safety-net academic institution and was published in the American Journal of Obstetrics & Gynecology MFM in 2022, volume 4, issue 5, article 100662.
